messages:
jamal: Evening handoff — quick heads up. I'm primary until 23:00 UTC tonight, but I have a personal appointment and there's a coverage gap from 23:00 -> 01:00 UTC. I can't extend. Can someone swap or pick up primary for that window?

oncall-bot: Reminder: please follow the handoff checklist: 1) state primary/secondary, 2) list active incidents, 3) note any in-flight deploys, 4) link runbooks. See https://redwood.app/runbooks/oncall-handoff

maria: I can take 23:00-00:30 UTC if that helps. I’ll be at my desk and can handle pages up to 20 concurrent requests. :thumbsup:

taylor: I can pick up 00:30-01:00 UTC but only if someone pages me with high priority — I won't be watching low-priority alerts while on commute. Please escalate to me for sev2+ after 00:30.

jamal: Perfect — plan: jamal primary until 23:00, maria primary 23:00-00:30, taylor primary 00:30-01:00, then jamal back at 01:00. I’ll update the rotation note and ping PagerDuty to reflect the swap.

alex: For anyone taking primary: quick escalation checklist (copy/paste into the handoff note):
```
- If alert is sev3: ack in PD, investigate 10m window, update ticket with initial triage.
- If sev2: page primary phone + escalate to SRE lead (pager: +1-555-211-SRE) immediately, open incident bridge, post to #incidents.
- If sev1: activate all-hands bridge, notify Eng CTL and on-call manager, follow the Sev1 runbook.
```
Also: when paging, call then PD message — sometimes PD messags are delayed.

incident-bot: Paging rules reminder: Sev2 = page primary + message on #incidents; if no ack in 5 minutes escalate to on-call-manager; Sev1 = immediate page to entire oncall-rotation and call ops-manager. See escalation matrix: https://redwood.app/paging-matrix

maria: quick Q — for customer-impact assessment, do we always use the short template or the full postmortem draft? Trying to triage how much detail to put in the incident description when I ack.

alex: Short template is fine during triage. Use this snippet in the PD entry: 
```
- Customer impact: yes/no + percent/region
- ETA for mitigation: rough minutes
- Actions taken: commands/runbook steps
- Next owner: who is driving
```
Follow up with the full postmortem only if the incident hits sev1 or repeated sev2 in 24h.

taylor: FYI there was some noisy cache-miss alerts on staging earlier — metrics look like increased miss rate on redis-proxy from 22:20 UTC. If you get pages about latency, start by checking redis-proxy and the prefix cache (dash: https://grafana.redwood/rd/cache-miss).

jamal: Good call. I'll add that to the handoff note under 'known issues'. Also flag: there's a canary deploy scheduled at 23:15 UTC for model-serving; if canary fails, the auto-fallback should kick in but watch for traffic spikes.

ops-bot: deploy: canary model-serving v2.3.1 started at 23:15 UTC — monitor rollback logs at /var/log/deploys/model-serving/canary.log

maria: thanks — I'll keep an eye on the canary during my shift segment. If I see more than 2% error rate for 3 consecutive minutes, I'll open a Sev2 and page.

jamal: Ok team — final check: @maria you own 23:00-00:30, @taylor you own 00:30-01:00. I'll update PagerDuty and the handoff doc now, leaving the 'known issues' + runbook links. Please ack here when you see the PD change.

maria: Acked and I can see the PD note.

taylor: Acked. I updated my phone number in PD.

jamal: Thanks everyone. If anything urgent during the gap, follow the escalation steps Alex posted. I'll be reachable by DM for critical stuff but prefer not to be paged unless it's sev2+. Leaving notes in the handoff doc now: https://redwood.app/handovers/1862504321-handoff
